    83	## 3. Mechanism mapping
    84	
    85	### B: Interrupt-driven PIR input (`pird`, `src/capture/pir`)
    86	**Implementation.** `pird` requests the PIR line through libgpiod v2 with both
    87	edges, pull-up bias, and kernel event timestamps (`CLOCK_MONOTONIC`). It blocks
    88	in the kernel until an edge arrives; the GPIO IRQ handler in the RP1 driver
    89	timestamps the edge and wakes us. A `--poll=<ms>` mode reads the line value on a
    90	`timerfd` instead and is the comparison arm.
    91	**Why Macy needs it.** The PIR changes state a few times a day, while the same
    92	four cores run audio FFTs every 20 ms and camera bursts. Spinning on a pin for
    93	an input that rarely changes takes CPU from the work that does. And the fusion window (Section 4) correlates a PIR edge with an audio
    94	transient within a second or two, so edge timestamps must be accurate to well
    95	under the 20 ms audio frame; a poll interval long enough to be cheap blurs that.
    96	**Measured.** Edge-to-userspace latency distribution and `pird` CPU utilization,
    97	IRQ vs. poll at 1, 10, 100 ms, idle and under `stress-ng` load (Section 9).
    98	
    99	### D: Custom storage layer (`src/store`, linked into `hub`)
   100	**Implementation.** Append-only, CRC32-framed event log in segment files;
   101	atomic clip commits (tmp → fsync → rename → fsync dir); startup recovery; a
   102	byte quota with oldest-first eviction. Details in Section 5.
   103	**Why Macy needs it.** The device runs from the room's wall outlet, and hotel
   104	outlets get used: housekeeping unplugs things to run a vacuum, Macy unplugs it
   105	to pack, a power strip gets kicked.
   106	The record exists to settle "did someone come in?" after the fact; a log that
   107	is corrupt or silently truncated after a power loss fails at the only moment it
   108	matters. The SD card is also small and wears, and clips are the bulk of writes
   109	(the memo's named risk).
   110	**Measured.** Power-pull recovery (records lost, records corrupt), write
   111	amplification and bytes/day, fsync count and latency.
   112	
   113	### E: Multi-process architecture with supervision (`src/supervisor`, `src/hub`)
   114	**Implementation.** One process per sensor, one hub, one supervisor. Children
   115	send a heartbeat every 5 s. The supervisor restarts any child that exits or
   116	misses heartbeats for 15 s (SIGKILL first), with exponential backoff 1 s → 60 s
   117	that resets after 10 min of health. Exit code `3` (device gone) is distinguished
   118	from a crash: the supervisor retries slowly and the hub enters a DEGRADED mode
   119	for that sensor instead of storming restarts.
   120	**Why Macy needs it.** A security monitor that silently dies is worse than none,
   121	because Macy believes it is on duty. If the camera stack hangs or the USB mic
   122	drops off the bus, the PIR record must keep flowing and the timeline must say
   123	plainly which sensors were offline and when.
   124	**Measured.** `kill -9` each child and unplug the mic during runs: detection
   125	time, recovery time, events lost during the gap, and the log excerpt.
   126	
   127	## 4. Analysis engine (`src/analysis`, all ours)
   128	
   129	**Audio features (in `micd`).** 20 ms hops (882 samples) over a 1024-point Hann
   130	window. Per frame: RMS, energy in 8 log-spaced bands (100 Hz – 8 kHz), and
   131	spectral flux (sum of positive band-energy increases). FFT via a small library
   132	or our own radix-2; either way it is a primitive we can explain.
   133	
   134	**Background model.** For each band, an exponentially weighted mean and
   135	variance (time constant ~60 s) updated only on frames not inside an active
   136	event, so a long conversation does not teach the model that voices are
   137	background. Each frame is scored as a per-band z-score. This is what lets the
   138	same device work next to a loud HVAC unit and in a silent room.
   139	
   140	**Detectors.**
   141	- *Impulse (latch/door):* spectral-flux z-score spike above `K_imp` with a short
   142	  decay (< 150 ms) and broadband energy, the shape of a latch or door thud.
   143	- *Voice:* z-score in the 300–3400 Hz bands above `K_voice` sustained for ≥ 400 ms
   144	  within a 2 s window, with low-band (< 200 Hz) energy not dominant (rules out HVAC).
   145	- *PIR:* rising edge debounced; HC-SR501's hardware block time (~2.5 s) and
   146	  retrigger mode noted in config.
   147	
   148	**Fusion state machine (in `hub`).**
   149	```
   150	IDLE --PIR rise--> MOTION_WINDOW (open ±T_co = 3 s around the edge, look back in audio history)
   151	MOTION_WINDOW --impulse or voice in window--> ENTRY (confirmed)
   152	MOTION_WINDOW --window expires, no audio--> MOTION_ONLY
   153	IDLE --impulse/voice with no PIR in ±T_co--> SOUND_ONLY (hallway)
   154	ENTRY/MOTION_ONLY --no PIR high and no voice for T_quiet = 30 s--> close event
   155	```
   156	An event records start, end, duration, which detectors fired, peak scores,
   157	sensors available (DEGRADED flags), and clip references. Opening and closing use
   158	different conditions (hysteresis), so a person moving around the room for ten
   159	minutes is one event, not forty.
   160	
   161	**Routine vs. unexpected.** Macy sets an expected window (`cli expect
   162	10:00-14:00`). Confirmed entries inside it are labelled `routine`; outside it,
   163	`UNEXPECTED`. The device does not try to identify who entered.
   164	
   165	**Why a threshold cannot do this.** A fixed loudness threshold fires on every
   166	slammed door in the hallway and misses a quiet entry in a noisy room; a PIR
   167	alone fires on curtains moved by HVAC and sunlight patches. The decision depends
   168	on the *temporal coincidence* of two different physical signals, scored against
   169	a background that the device learned in *this* room, with hysteresis for event
   170	boundaries. Each piece is simple; no single `if` reproduces the combination.
   171	
   172	## 5. Storage and data
   173	
   174	| Data | Rate | Format | Retention |
   175	|---|---|---|---|
   176	| Event records | ~0.1–20 /hr | binary, `[len u32][type u16][ver u16][payload][crc32]` | quota-managed, never evicted before clips |
   177	| Stats / heartbeat records | 1 /min, batched | same framing | 7 days |
   178	| Audio clips (confirmed entries only) | 10 s pre-roll + ≤ 20 s post, 88.2 KB/s ≈ 2.6 MB | WAV | quota (oldest first) |
   179	| Image bursts (confirmed entries only) | ~2 fps × 10 s, ~150–300 KB each ≈ 3–6 MB | JPEG | quota (oldest first) |
   180	| Daemon text logs | low | line-oriented, timestamped | logrotate by size, 4 × 5 MB |
   181	
   182	**Event log.** Segment files `log/seg-NNNNNN.pel` capped at 4 MB. Records are
   183	appended with `write()` and the segment is `fdatasync`ed when an event *closes*
   184	(low rate, so per-event durability is affordable). Stats records are buffered
   185	in memory and flushed once a minute, so a power cut loses at most a minute of
   186	stats but never a closed event.
   187	
   188	**Clips.** Written as `clips/<event-id>.{wav,dir}.tmp`; on completion: `fsync`
   189	file → `rename` to final name → `fsync` the directory. The event record that
   190	references a clip is written only after the rename is durable, so the log never
   191	points at a missing clip. Unconfirmed bursts (MOTION_ONLY / SOUND_ONLY) are
   192	deleted, not kept. That is the main defence against the memo's storage risk.
   193	
   194	**Recovery (at hub start).** Scan the newest segment; stop at the first record
   195	with a bad length or CRC; `ftruncate` there; log `store: recovered seg=N
   196	valid=R truncated_bytes=B`. Delete every `*.tmp` in `clips/` and log each one.
   197	Rebuild the in-memory index (event id → offset) from the segments.
   198	
   199	**Power-loss gaps.** The hub writes a `boot` record at every start. Stats
   200	records land once a minute, so the span between the last durable record and the
   201	`boot` record is when the device was off, accurate to about a minute. `timeline`
   202	shows that span as an `OFFLINE` line, so Macy knows the device was not watching
   203	then, instead of reading silence as "nobody came in".
   204	
   205	**Quota.** Default 2 GiB for `clips/`. Before a new clip, evict the oldest clips
   206	until there is room. At ~6–9 MB per confirmed entry, that is ~250 entries,
   207	several trips' worth. A free-space floor (5 % of the filesystem) stops all clip
   208	writes before the card fills, while event records still go through.
   209	
   210	**Time.** There is no NTP offline. Wall-clock timestamps come from the Pi 5's
   211	RTC (with its backup battery fitted) or `cli settime`; every interval and
   212	ordering decision uses `CLOCK_MONOTONIC`. Records carry both, so a wrong wall
   213	clock can be corrected after the fact without reordering events.
   214	
   215	## 6. Failure-mode table
   216	
   217	| Component | Failure | Detected by | System response | Log shows |
   218	|---|---|---|---|---|
   219	| `micd` | Snowball unplugged | ALSA read returns `-ENODEV`/`-EIO` | exit 3; supervisor retries every 30 s; hub marks audio DEGRADED; fusion falls back to PIR-only, events tagged `unconfirmed (audio offline)` | `micd: snd_pcm_readi: No such device; exit 3` / `sup: micd device-gone, retry 30s` / `hub: DEGRADED audio` … `hub: RECOVERED audio after 612s` |
   220	| `micd` | crash / `kill -9` | `SIGCHLD` + `waitpid` status | restart with backoff; events during gap tagged DEGRADED | `sup: micd killed by signal 9, restart #3 in 1s` |
   221	| `micd` | ALSA overrun (xrun) | `-EPIPE` from read | `snd_pcm_prepare`, count it, continue | `micd: xrun #N recovered` (counted in heartbeat) |
   222	| `pird` | crash / hang | `SIGCHLD` / missed heartbeat 15 s | SIGKILL + restart; hub marks PIR DEGRADED | `sup: pird heartbeat missed 15s, SIGKILL` |
   223	| PIR sensor | unplugged | line held high by pull-up for > 300 s with no voice activity (**heuristic**: a person in constant motion could also do this) | flag PIR `SUSPECT`, keep running, surface in `status` | `pird: line stuck high 300s, SUSPECT` |
   224	| PIR sensor | warm-up false triggers (first ~60 s after power) | uptime < 60 s | ignore edges during warm-up | `pird: warm-up, edges ignored until T+60s` |
   225	| `camd` | `rpicam-still` fails / camera absent | non-zero child exit, missing files | event kept without images, tagged `no-images`; camd backoff | `camd: rpicam-still exit 255; burst skipped` |
   226	| `camd` | crash / `kill -9` | `SIGCHLD` | restart; in-flight `.tmp` burst cleaned on next start | `sup: camd killed by signal 9` |
   227	| `hub` | crash / `kill -9` | `SIGCHLD` | restart; recovery scan runs; sensor daemons reconnect (they retry connect with backoff and drop frames while disconnected, counted) | `store: recovered seg=12 valid=341 truncated_bytes=58` |
   228	| storage | power cut mid-write | CRC/length check at startup | truncate torn tail, delete `.tmp` clips | as above |
   229	| power | device unplugged (housekeeping, Macy, or an intruder) | at next boot: gap between last durable record and new `boot` record | timeline shows an `OFFLINE` span; nothing is recorded while off | `hub: boot after power loss, offline 10:02-10:40 (38m)` |
   230	| storage | disk near full | `statvfs` before each clip | stop clips, keep events, raise `health` warning | `store: free 4.8% < floor, clips disabled` |
   231	| storage | `write`/`fsync` error (EIO) | syscall return | log, retry once, then exit non-zero so supervisor restarts hub | `store: fdatasync: Input/output error` |
   232	| `supervisor` | itself killed | systemd (`Restart=always`) | systemd restarts it; it kills stale children via the pidfile/process group before relaunching | `sup: start, cleaned 3 stale children` |
   233	| any child | fd leak across restarts | hourly heartbeat records `/proc/<pid>/fd` count | soak evidence; regression test | `hb: ... fds=pird:5 micd:7 ...` |
   234	
   235	## 7. Interface: CLI (`src/cli`)
   236	
   237	Offline only: the CLI runs on the Pi (local console or USB-serial) and talks to
   238	the hub over `/run/pss/query.sock`. Four verbs, each with exact semantics:
   239	
   240	```
   241	$ pss timeline [--since 08:00] [--until now]     # human-readable, one line per event
   242	09:41:07  ENTRY       routine     4m12s  latch+voice  [12 imgs, 30s audio]
   243	12:03:55  SOUND_ONLY  -             6s   voice        hallway?
   244	13:10:02  OFFLINE     -           38m   -            power lost
   245	15:22:40  ENTRY       UNEXPECTED   38s  latch         [20 imgs, 30s audio]
   246	
   247	$ pss events [--type entry|motion|sound] [--json]   # full records incl. scores, sensor flags
   248	$ pss status                                        # armed?, expected window, sensors OK/DEGRADED/SUSPECT
   249	$ pss health                                        # per-process uptime, restarts, RSS, fds, disk free, xruns, drops
   250	```
   251	Plus two setters: `pss expect HH:MM-HH:MM` and `pss settime`.
   252	
   253	## 8. Constraints and substitutions
   254	
   255	| Ideal | What we use | What it costs us |
   256	|---|---|---|
   257	| Small embedded I2S MEMS mic | Blue Snowball USB mic (owned) | Bulky; USB audio adds latency and xruns are possible; but unplugging it is a clean, safe fault to inject and demo |
   258	| Door reed switch for automatic ground truth | None installed (it is Macy's hotel door, not ours) | Ground truth comes from scripted trials and a paper log with timestamps; fewer labels and more effort |
   259	| Continuous video with pre-roll | JPEG still bursts on PIR trigger | Pi 5 has no hardware H.264 encoder; software video would take a large share of the CPU that audio analysis needs. We miss the first ~1 s (camera start latency, measured) and get frames, not motion |
   260	| Camera in the fusion | Camera as evidence only | We run no vision models (no pretrained models allowed and no budget to write one); images are for Macy to look at |
   261	| Battery power, so it can sit anywhere in the room | Wall outlet via a Pi 5 USB-C supply (5 V / 5 A) | Must sit within cable reach of an outlet; anyone, housekeeping included, can unplug it. That is a power cut, hence D and the `OFFLINE` gap record (Section 5) |
   262	| Reliable PIR-disconnect detection | Pull-up "stuck high" heuristic | Can be fooled; stated as a limitation |
   263	| Real hotel rooms | One test room (dorm/apartment) with a door | Acoustics and hallway noise are not a hotel's; claim narrowed accordingly |
   264	
   265	Replayed data: we will record labelled audio/PIR traces from scripted trials and
   266	replay them through `micd`'s feature path and the hub (`tools/replay`) to tune
   267	`K_imp`, `K_voice`, and `T_co`. Replayed data is labelled as such everywhere it
   268	appears; the soak and the demo run on live sensors.
   269	
   270	## 9. Evaluation plan
   271	
   272	| Measurement | Method | Target |
   273	|---|---|---|
   274	| **B: PIR latency, IRQ vs. poll** | Drive a spare GPIO output into the PIR input line (PIR disconnected); toggle with a timestamp from the same monotonic clock; compute toggle → `pird` receipt. 1,000 edges per arm; arms: IRQ, poll 1/10/100 ms; idle and under `stress-ng --cpu 4` | IRQ p99 < 1 ms idle, < 5 ms loaded; report full CDFs |
   275	| **B: CPU cost** | `pird` CPU from `/proc/<pid>/stat` over 10 min each arm | IRQ ≈ 0 %; report poll cost |
   276	| **Detection accuracy (domain metric)** | ≥ 30 scripted trials each: real entry (door + walk in), housekeeping-style long entry, hallway noise only, non-human motion (fan-blown curtain), empty room. Paper log for ground truth | Confusion matrix; entry recall ≥ 90 %, false ENTRY on non-entry trials ≤ 5 % |
   277	| **Event-to-record latency** | PIR edge timestamp → event record durable | p95 < 5 s after window closes |
   278	| **D: power-cut recovery** | 20 power pulls at random times during clip and log writes | 0 corrupt records accepted; 0 dangling clip refs; lost data ≤ last open event |
   279	| **D: write volume** | bytes written per day from `/proc/<pid>/io` and `/sys/block/mmcblk0/stat` | report; < 1 GB/day at 20 entries/day |
   280	| **E: fault recovery** | `kill -9` each child 10×; unplug mic 10× for 10 min | detection < 1 s (crash) / < 15 s (hang); restart < 5 s; no fd growth |
   281	| **Camera start latency** | PIR edge → first JPEG mtime | report distribution (expected ~1 s) |
   282	| **Resource footprint** | hourly heartbeats over the 48 h soak: RSS, CPU, fds per process | flat RSS (< 1 MB drift after warm-up); plotted |
   283	
   284	## 10. Ownership map
   285	
   286	Owners are **to be decided by the team**; this table is the list to assign.
   287	Ownership means first authorship and answerability at the defense.
   288	
   289	| Subsystem | Path | Owner |
   290	|---|---|---|
   291	| PIR capture + IRQ/poll comparison (B) | `src/capture/pir` | TBD |
   292	| Microphone capture + feature extraction | `src/capture/mic` | TBD |
   293	| Camera burst capture | `src/capture/cam` | TBD |
   294	| Storage layer (D) | `src/store` | TBD |
   295	| Analysis: background model, detectors, fusion FSM | `src/analysis` | TBD |
   296	| Hub (event loop, IPC server, query handling) | `src/hub` | Shared |
   297	| Supervisor (E) | `src/supervisor` | Shared |
   298	| CLI | `src/cli` | Shared |
   299	| Replay harness, plotting | `tools/` | TBD |
   300	
   301	Once decided, the same split goes into CLAUDE.md's Ownership section.
   302	
   303	## 11. AI-use plan and the no-network boundary
   304	
   305	**We use Claude Code for:** planning (plan mode first for every multi-file
   306	change), explaining APIs (libgpiod v2, ALSA, epoll, signalfd), drafting
   307	boilerplate, writing tests and fixtures, adversarial review of diffs, and
   308	debugging with pasted evidence (dmesg, `/proc/interrupts`, timing captures).
   309	**We do not use it for:** choosing detector thresholds or fusion rules without
   310	data we collected, or anything that runs on the device at runtime.
   311	
   312	**Boundary, legible in one minute.** The product links no network library and
   313	opens only AF_UNIX sockets. `make netcheck` greps `src/` for `AF_INET`,
   314	`AF_INET6`, `getaddrinfo`, `connect(` outside `AF_UNIX` helpers, `curl`, and
   315	`http`, and fails the build if any appear. The device runs with Wi-Fi and
   316	Ethernet disabled during the soak, which is the strongest possible check.
   317	
   318	## 12. Proposed repository layout
   319	
   320	```
   321	src/capture/{pir,mic,cam}/   sensor daemons
   322	src/analysis/                features, background model, detectors, fusion
   323	src/store/                   event log, clip store, recovery, quota
   324	src/hub/                     event loop, IPC, query server
   325	src/supervisor/              process supervision, soak heartbeat
   326	src/cli/                     pss command
   327	src/common/                  IPC message structs, logging, heartbeat client
   328	tests/                       unit tests (store recovery, FSM, ring), run by `make test`
   329	tools/                       Python: replay harness, plotting (no graded mechanism)
   330	deploy/                      systemd unit for supervisor
   331	```

I read the handout and all your files: [Problem-Memo.md](Problem-Memo.md), [Design.md](Design.md), [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md), the README, and the git log. The design is strong overall. B, D and E are justified from Macy's situation, the failure table is honest, and the claim is narrowed well. But there are three problems that could cost real points, plus several design holes and inconsistencies.

## Could cost points

1. **Shared sessions break the transcript grade.** My saved notes say you and Bryan often prompt together in one session. The handout says sessions are personal and that "working in one shared login … will cost both partners." Your 10 process points come from your own transcripts, checked against your own commits. Right now Bryan has one commit and no transcripts. Each of you needs your own clone and your own Claude Code sessions starting now. Store transcripts per person, e.g. `CLAUDE-TRANSCRIPTS/owen/` and `CLAUDE-TRANSCRIPTS/bryan/`.

2. **Macy has no realistic way to read the timeline.** The CLI only runs on "local console or USB-serial," so Macy would need a monitor and keyboard, or a serial cable and a laptop, in a hotel room. The handout allows serving your own LAN interface. The Pi 5 could run its own Wi-Fi access point and serve the timeline locally, which is still offline. As written, the product's whole answer is locked behind a debugging cable.

3. **There's no arm/disarm.** Every time Macy comes back, and every night she sleeps there, the device logs an `UNEXPECTED` entry. `pss status` shows "armed?" but no command sets it. Without one, nearly every alert is a false alarm caused by Macy herself. That's the same failure that makes a wellness monitor get unplugged in Seed 1.

## Design holes

4. **An intruder who unplugs the device erases their own entry.** The log is only fsynced when an event closes, after 30 s of quiet. If someone enters, sets off ENTRY, then pulls the plug, the event was never made durable. This is the exact threat you name in §3 D. Fix: write and fsync an "entry opened" record the moment ENTRY is confirmed, then a close record later.

5. **Unplugging the PIR creates a fake event, and detection takes 5 minutes.** With pull-up bias, pulling the PIR's signal wire makes the line go high. That looks like a rising edge, which opens a motion window. Then "stuck high" takes 300 s to flag. On demo day the grader unplugs a sensor and expects the system to notice. Either decide which sensor you'll hand them, or find a faster PIR-loss signal.

6. **Some sensors aren't safe to unplug while powered.** The CSI camera ribbon must not be pulled with power on. The PIR's bare 5 V jumper wires are the hot-plug hazard the handout warns about. Put the PIR on a keyed connector, and make sure the mic and PIR are the "unplug me" sensors.

7. **Stats retention and event retention conflict.** Stats records (kept 7 days) and events (never evicted before clips) share the same append-only segments. You can't drop old stats from a segment without dropping the events in it. Split them into separate logs or define how compaction works.

8. **The RTC battery is load-bearing, and the plan doesn't say you have one.** `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` resets every boot, so the `OFFLINE` span and every timestamp after a power cut depend on the Pi 5 RTC battery. It's sold separately. Buy it, or say that offline spans are unknown without it.

9. **The latency argument for B is weak.** You justify interrupts by needing edge timestamps "well under 20 ms," but the fusion window is ±3 s. The HC-SR501 itself takes hundreds of ms to react, and a 100 ms poll costs almost no CPU. The defense will test this. A better story would be the RT/load comparison, or simply that interrupts give kernel timestamps on edges you'd otherwise miss between polls. Be ready to admit the CPU gap is tiny.

10. **The audio pre-roll is short.** The PCM ring holds 10 s, but confirmation comes about 3 s after the PIR edge. You can't get a full 10 s of pre-roll. Make the ring about 15 s or change the number.

## Inconsistencies across files

- **CLAUDE.md is mostly the handout's sample copied as-is.**
  - It still says `alice/` and `bob/`.
  - It lists `src/drv`, but you have no driver since mechanism A wasn't chosen.
  - It mentions a "LAN interface" your design doesn't have.
  - It lacks `make netcheck`, the camera, wall power, and the RTC.
  - It uses curly quotes (‘make‘) instead of backticks.
- **Ownership is decided in one place and open in another.** CLAUDE.md assigns capture to one person and store/analysis to the other, while Design §10 says "TBD." Pick one answer and put real names in both files.
- **The memo and the design describe the problem differently.** The memo says "three sensors, B + D"; the design says "two cooperating + one evidence, B + D + E." Changing is allowed, but the M5 changelog should say so. The memo also switches between "they" and "her" for Macy and has a stray `>` in the title.
- **"Portable" vs. wall power.** The name says portable, but the device now needs an outlet. That's fine, but say why in one line.

## Things a skeptical reader will ask

- **Why not an old phone with an offline motion-detection app, or a $15 travel door alarm?** The memo only rules out cloud cameras. Answer the cheaper alternatives directly.
- **Is recording audio legal here?** Recording voices of hotel staff without consent is restricted in some places (two-party consent laws). Also, Seed 3 praises *not* having a camera. Address both, e.g. "audio is analyzed, not kept" or "clips only on confirmed UNEXPECTED entries."
- **How does Macy know the housekeeping window?** Housekeeping times usually aren't known in advance.

## Smaller items

- **Design.md is too long.** It's about 3,500 words, likely 7+ pages against a 3–5 page limit. Trim, or move tables to an appendix.
- **File names don't match the deliverable list.** The handout asks for `PROBLEM.md` and `DESIGN.md`, not `Problem-Memo.md` / `Design.md`.
- **The `make netcheck` grep for `http` will trip on comments and URLs.** Narrow the pattern.
- **Some hardware facts need checking on the bench:**
  - whether the Snowball records mono or stereo (`arecord --dump-hw-params`)
  - whether your OV5647 came with a Pi 5 cable (the Pi 5 needs a 22-pin cable)
- **M2 also requires both sensors working on real hardware.** Nothing in the repo shows that yet. Commit a capture log or dmesg output.
- **The README is empty.**
- **There are 4 commits so far against the 40 required,** and only 1 is Bryan's.

I didn't change any files. Items 1–4 are the ones I'd fix before M2 is graded. Want me to draft the CLAUDE.md cleanup and the arm/disarm plus durable-entry changes to the design?

## Plan

**Renames** (with `git mv`, so file history is kept)
- `Problem-Memo.md` → `PROBLEM.md`
- `Design.md` → `DESIGN.md`

**[CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md)**
- Fix the curly quotes so commands use normal backticks.
- Ownership: Owen gets `src/capture/{pir,mic,cam}` and the button; Bryan gets `src/store` and `src/analysis`. Hub, supervisor, CLI/UI are shared. Remove `src/drv` and the alice/bob names.
- Add a rule that each partner uses their own clone and their own Claude Code sessions, with transcripts copied to `CLAUDE-TRANSCRIPTS/<name>/`.
- Add `make netcheck`. Reword the network rule so the only allowed network code is the local hotspot interface.
- Add short project facts: wall power, RTC battery, which sensors are safe to unplug.

**PROBLEM.md**
- Fix the title typo and use her/she for Macy throughout.
- Add one or two sentences on why an old phone app or a $15 door alarm doesn't solve this.
- Note the sensors and mechanisms changed in the design (three sensors, mechanisms B, D, E).

**DESIGN.md**

*New features*
- **Arm/disarm:** a GPIO button plus LED handled by `pird`, with a 60 s exit delay and a 30 s re-entry grace period. Events while disarmed aren't flagged. Add a matching `pss arm`/`pss disarm` and `status` field.
- **Interface:** the Pi runs its own Wi-Fi hotspot with no internet. Macy joins from her phone and sees a timeline page served on that interface only. `pss` still works over SSH. The query logic stays in C; anything under `ui/` is only a display layer.
- **Section 11 rewrite:** the server listens only on the hotspot address, and `netcheck` allows exactly that one server file. "Wi-Fi off during soak" becomes "hotspot on, no internet connection."

*Fixes to existing parts*
- **Unplugging the device mid-entry:** write and fsync an "entry opened" record as soon as an ENTRY is confirmed, and a "closed" record later. Recovery marks an entry with no close record as "interrupted (power lost)."
- **PIR unplug:** wire it with a keyed connector. Note in the design that pulling it causes one false edge, and log that as a possible unplug when the line then stays high. The mic is the sensor we offer for demo-day unplugging; the camera is marked never hot-unplug.
- **Storage:** stats/heartbeats go in their own log segments so they can be deleted after 7 days without touching events.
- **Time:** the RTC battery becomes a stated requirement. Without it, the device marks offline spans as "duration unknown."
- **Audio buffer:** grow it from 10 s to 15 s so a full 10 s pre-roll exists after the ~3 s confirmation delay.

*Wording changes*
- **Mechanism B case:** replace the "timestamps under 20 ms" argument with an honest one. Interrupts catch every edge with a kernel timestamp, including short pulses a poll can miss, at near-zero CPU. We expect the CPU gap to be small and will report it either way. The button is a second interrupt input.
- **Privacy:** keep audio and image clips as designed, add a short privacy/consent paragraph, and add a row to the constraints table.
- **Housekeeping window:** add a sentence saying it's optional; with arming, any confirmed entry while armed is reported.
- **Length:** tighten the text to fit 3–5 pages, about 2,500 words. Tables stay; prose gets shortened.

**Not doing**
- README, real-hardware evidence, and the commit count. These need actual code and a working Pi.
- Committing. I'll leave it for you to review.

lines: +# Design Document: Portable Security (Owen Pendleton, Bryan Rosas)
+**Milestone:** M2. **Status:** draft for review. This document will change as we
+meet the hardware; M5's version will carry a changelog of what this one got wrong.
+## 1. Summary
+Macy travels about three nights a month and leaves a laptop, cash, and bags in a
+hotel room all day. Our device sits in the room while she is out and, when she
+returns, answers one question with a short timeline: *did anyone come in, when,
+and for how long?* It runs fully offline (no Wi-Fi, no cloud, no account) and
+keeps every byte on its own SD card.
+**The narrowed claim we will defend:** on our hardware, in a test room, the
+device separates *door-entry events* (motion plus a door/voice sound signature)
+from *motion-only* and *sound-only* events with a measured confusion matrix,
+labels each entry routine or unexpected against a housekeeping window Macy sets,
+and keeps a crash-consistent record of it through power cuts and sensor faults.
+**Mechanisms (Section 3.2 menu):** **B** interrupt-driven PIR input, compared
+head-to-head with polling; **D** a custom crash-consistent storage layer; **E** a
+multi-process architecture with a supervisor that survives any child dying.
+**Hardware:** Raspberry Pi 5 · HC-SR501 PIR (GPIO) · Blue Snowball USB
+microphone (ALSA) · Arducam 5MP OV5647 camera (CSI, via `rpicam-*` tools).
+PIR and microphone are the two *cooperating* sensors; the camera is an evidence
+sensor that is triggered by the PIR and kept only when fusion confirms an entry.
+## 2. Architecture
+ HC-SR501 PIR          Blue Snowball (USB)        Arducam OV5647 (CSI)
+     | GPIO edge            | USB isoc audio            | CSI-2
+ RP1 gpiochip            snd-usb-audio             libcamera / rpicam-*
+ (line-edge events,      (ALSA PCM, 44.1 kHz       (JPEG stills on demand)
+  kernel timestamps)      s16 mono = 88.2 KB/s)
+     v                      v                           v
+ |  pird  |           |   micd    |              |   camd    |
+ | B: IRQ |           | 20 ms FFT |              | burst on  |
+ | or poll|           | features; |              | trigger;  |
+     | (<1 Hz typ,         | feature frames         |     | frame-ready msgs
+     |  ~40 B each)        | 50 Hz x ~64 B          |     | (2 Hz, path only)
+     v                     v                        |     v
+ |                         hub (single writer)                    |
+ |  analysis/: background model -> detectors -> fusion FSM        |
+ |  store/:    event log (append, CRC) + clip store (quota)       |
+ |  query socket for cli                                          |
+     |  writes: event records ~0.1-20/hr, fsync per closed event
+     |          clips ~6-9 MB per confirmed entry
+     |          stats/heartbeat records batched, 1/min
+     v
+ SD card: /var/lib/pss/{log/, clips/, state/}
+ supervisor (E): fork/execs pird, micd, camd, hub; reaps with waitpid;
+ receives 5 s heartbeats from each child over AF_UNIX; writes the hourly
+ soak heartbeat (liveness, RSS, event counts) to its own log.
+ cli  --AF_UNIX query socket-->  hub      (timeline, events, status, health)
+All IPC is AF_UNIX `SOCK_SEQPACKET`: message boundaries are preserved, and a
+dead peer shows up as EOF/EPIPE, which is exactly the fault signal E needs.
+The product opens no AF_INET socket anywhere (Section 11).
+| Process | Threads | Priority | Inputs → outputs |
+| `supervisor` | 1 (epoll loop: signalfd, child sockets, timerfd) | default | heartbeats → restarts, soak log |
+| `pird` | 1 (blocks in `gpiod_line_request_read_edge_events` or poll timer) | default (C is not claimed) | GPIO → edge msgs |
+| `micd` | 2: ALSA capture thread, feature thread, joined by an SPSC ring | default | PCM → feature frames, audio clip on request |
+| `camd` | 1 + `rpicam-still` child per burst | default | trigger → JPEG files in `clips/*.tmp` |
+| `hub` | 1 (epoll loop over all child sockets + query socket + timerfd) | default | features + edges → events, storage |
+| `cli` | 1, short-lived | n/a | user query → text |
+## 3. Mechanism mapping
+### B: Interrupt-driven PIR input (`pird`, `src/capture/pir`)
+**Implementation.** `pird` requests the PIR line through libgpiod v2 with both
+edges, pull-up bias, and kernel event timestamps (`CLOCK_MONOTONIC`). It blocks
+in the kernel until an edge arrives; the GPIO IRQ handler in the RP1 driver
+timestamps the edge and wakes us. A `--poll=<ms>` mode reads the line value on a
+`timerfd` instead and is the comparison arm.
+**Why Macy needs it.** The PIR changes state a few times a day, while the same
+four cores run audio FFTs every 20 ms and camera bursts. Spinning on a pin for
+an input that rarely changes takes CPU from the work that does. And the fusion window (Section 4) correlates a PIR edge with an audio
+transient within a second or two, so edge timestamps must be accurate to well
+under the 20 ms audio frame; a poll interval long enough to be cheap blurs that.
+**Measured.** Edge-to-userspace latency distribution and `pird` CPU utilization,
+IRQ vs. poll at 1, 10, 100 ms, idle and under `stress-ng` load (Section 9).
+### D: Custom storage layer (`src/store`, linked into `hub`)
+**Implementation.** Append-only, CRC32-framed event log in segment files;
+atomic clip commits (tmp → fsync → rename → fsync dir); startup recovery; a
+byte quota with oldest-first eviction. Details in Section 5.
+**Why Macy needs it.** The device runs from the room's wall outlet, and hotel
+outlets get used: housekeeping unplugs things to run a vacuum, Macy unplugs it
+to pack, a power strip gets kicked.
+The record exists to settle "did someone come in?" after the fact; a log that
+is corrupt or silently truncated after a power loss fails at the only moment it
+matters. The SD card is also small and wears, and clips are the bulk of writes
+(the memo's named risk).
+**Measured.** Power-pull recovery (records lost, records corrupt), write
+amplification and bytes/day, fsync count and latency.
+### E: Multi-process architecture with supervision (`src/supervisor`, `src/hub`)
+**Implementation.** One process per sensor, one hub, one supervisor. Children
+send a heartbeat every 5 s. The supervisor restarts any child that exits or
+misses heartbeats for 15 s (SIGKILL first), with exponential backoff 1 s → 60 s
+that resets after 10 min of health. Exit code `3` (device gone) is distinguished
+from a crash: the supervisor retries slowly and the hub enters a DEGRADED mode
+for that sensor instead of storming restarts.
+**Why Macy needs it.** A security monitor that silently dies is worse than none,
+because Macy believes it is on duty. If the camera stack hangs or the USB mic
+drops off the bus, the PIR record must keep flowing and the timeline must say
+plainly which sensors were offline and when.
+**Measured.** `kill -9` each child and unplug the mic during runs: detection
+time, recovery time, events lost during the gap, and the log excerpt.
+## 4. Analysis engine (`src/analysis`, all ours)
+**Audio features (in `micd`).** 20 ms hops (882 samples) over a 1024-point Hann
+window. Per frame: RMS, energy in 8 log-spaced bands (100 Hz – 8 kHz), and
+spectral flux (sum of positive band-energy increases). FFT via a small library
+or our own radix-2; either way it is a primitive we can explain.
+**Background model.** For each band, an exponentially weighted mean and
+variance (time constant ~60 s) updated only on frames not inside an active
+event, so a long conversation does not teach the model that voices are
+background. Each frame is scored as a per-band z-score. This is what lets the
+same device work next to a loud HVAC unit and in a silent room.
+**Detectors.**
+- *Impulse (latch/door):* spectral-flux z-score spike above `K_imp` with a short
+  decay (< 150 ms) and broadband energy, the shape of a latch or door thud.
+- *Voice:* z-score in the 300–3400 Hz bands above `K_voice` sustained for ≥ 400 ms
+  within a 2 s window, with low-band (< 200 Hz) energy not dominant (rules out HVAC).
+- *PIR:* rising edge debounced; HC-SR501's hardware block time (~2.5 s) and
+  retrigger mode noted in config.
+**Fusion state machine (in `hub`).**
+IDLE --PIR rise--> MOTION_WINDOW (open ±T_co = 3 s around the edge, look back in audio history)
+MOTION_WINDOW --impulse or voice in window--> ENTRY (confirmed)
+MOTION_WINDOW --window expires, no audio--> MOTION_ONLY
+IDLE --impulse/voice with no PIR in ±T_co--> SOUND_ONLY (hallway)
+ENTRY/MOTION_ONLY --no PIR high and no voice for T_quiet = 30 s--> close event
+An event records start, end, duration, which detectors fired, peak scores,
+sensors available (DEGRADED flags), and clip references. Opening and closing use
+different conditions (hysteresis), so a person moving around the room for ten
+minutes is one event, not forty.
+**Routine vs. unexpected.** Macy sets an expected window (`cli expect
+10:00-14:00`). Confirmed entries inside it are labelled `routine`; outside it,
+`UNEXPECTED`. The device does not try to identify who entered.
+**Why a threshold cannot do this.** A fixed loudness threshold fires on every
+slammed door in the hallway and misses a quiet entry in a noisy room; a PIR
+alone fires on curtains moved by HVAC and sunlight patches. The decision depends
+on the *temporal coincidence* of two different physical signals, scored against
+a background that the device learned in *this* room, with hysteresis for event
+boundaries. Each piece is simple; no single `if` reproduces the combination.
+## 5. Storage and data
+| Data | Rate | Format | Retention |
+| Event records | ~0.1–20 /hr | binary, `[len u32][type u16][ver u16][payload][crc32]` | quota-managed, never evicted before clips |
+| Stats / heartbeat records | 1 /min, batched | same framing | 7 days |
+| Audio clips (confirmed entries only) | 10 s pre-roll + ≤ 20 s post, 88.2 KB/s ≈ 2.6 MB | WAV | quota (oldest first) |
+| Image bursts (confirmed entries only) | ~2 fps × 10 s, ~150–300 KB each ≈ 3–6 MB | JPEG | quota (oldest first) |
+| Daemon text logs | low | line-oriented, timestamped | logrotate by size, 4 × 5 MB |
+**Event log.** Segment files `log/seg-NNNNNN.pel` capped at 4 MB. Records are
+appended with `write()` and the segment is `fdatasync`ed when an event *closes*
+(low rate, so per-event durability is affordable). Stats records are buffered
+in memory and flushed once a minute, so a power cut loses at most a minute of
+stats but never a closed event.
+**Clips.** Written as `clips/<event-id>.{wav,dir}.tmp`; on completion: `fsync`
+file → `rename` to final name → `fsync` the directory. The event record that
+references a clip is written only after the rename is durable, so the log never
+points at a missing clip. Unconfirmed bursts (MOTION_ONLY / SOUND_ONLY) are
+deleted, not kept. That is the main defence against the memo's storage risk.
+**Recovery (at hub start).** Scan the newest segment; stop at the first record
+with a bad length or CRC; `ftruncate` there; log `store: recovered seg=N
+valid=R truncated_bytes=B`. Delete every `*.tmp` in `clips/` and log each one.
+Rebuild the in-memory index (event id → offset) from the segments.
+**Power-loss gaps.** The hub writes a `boot` record at every start. Stats
+records land once a minute, so the span between the last durable record and the
+`boot` record is when the device was off, accurate to about a minute. `timeline`
+shows that span as an `OFFLINE` line, so Macy knows the device was not watching
+then, instead of reading silence as "nobody came in".
+**Quota.** Default 2 GiB for `clips/`. Before a new clip, evict the oldest clips
+until there is room. At ~6–9 MB per confirmed entry, that is ~250 entries,
+several trips' worth. A free-space floor (5 % of the filesystem) stops all clip
+writes before the card fills, while event records still go through.
+**Time.** There is no NTP offline. Wall-clock timestamps come from the Pi 5's
+RTC (with its backup battery fitted) or `cli settime`; every interval and
+ordering decision uses `CLOCK_MONOTONIC`. Records carry both, so a wrong wall
+clock can be corrected after the fact without reordering events.
+## 6. Failure-mode table
+| Component | Failure | Detected by | System response | Log shows |

+| `micd` | Snowball unplugged | ALSA read returns `-ENODEV`/`-EIO` | exit 3; supervisor retries every 30 s; hub marks audio DEGRADED; fusion falls back to PIR-only, events tagged `unconfirmed (audio offline)` | `micd: snd_pcm_readi: No such device; exit 3` / `sup: micd device-gone, retry 30s` / `hub: DEGRADED audio` … `hub: RECOVERED audio after 612s` |
+| `micd` | crash / `kill -9` | `SIGCHLD` + `waitpid` status | restart with backoff; events during gap tagged DEGRADED | `sup: micd killed by signal 9, restart #3 in 1s` |
+| `micd` | ALSA overrun (xrun) | `-EPIPE` from read | `snd_pcm_prepare`, count it, continue | `micd: xrun #N recovered` (counted in heartbeat) |
+| `pird` | crash / hang | `SIGCHLD` / missed heartbeat 15 s | SIGKILL + restart; hub marks PIR DEGRADED | `sup: pird heartbeat missed 15s, SIGKILL` |

+| PIR sensor | unplugged | line held high by pull-up for > 300 s with no voice activity (**heuristic**: a person in constant motion could also do this) | flag PIR `SUSPECT`, keep running, surface in `status` | `pird: line stuck high 300s, SUSPECT` |
+| PIR sensor | warm-up false triggers (first ~60 s after power) | uptime < 60 s | ignore edges during warm-up | `pird: warm-up, edges ignored until T+60s` |
+| `camd` | `rpicam-still` fails / camera absent | non-zero child exit, missing files | event kept without images, tagged `no-images`; camd backoff | `camd: rpicam-still exit 255; burst skipped` |
+| `camd` | crash / `kill -9` | `SIGCHLD` | restart; in-flight `.tmp` burst cleaned on next start | `sup: camd killed by signal 9` |

+| `hub` | crash / `kill -9` | `SIGCHLD` | restart; recovery scan runs; sensor daemons reconnect (they retry connect with backoff and drop frames while disconnected, counted) | `store: recovered seg=12 valid=341 truncated_bytes=58` |
+| storage | power cut mid-write | CRC/length check at startup | truncate torn tail, delete `.tmp` clips | as above |

+| power | device unplugged (housekeeping, Macy, or an intruder) | at next boot: gap between last durable record and new `boot` record | timeline shows an `OFFLINE` span; nothing is recorded while off | `hub: boot after power loss, offline 10:02-10:40 (38m)` |
+| storage | disk near full | `statvfs` before each clip | stop clips, keep events, raise `health` warning | `store: free 4.8% < floor, clips disabled` |
+| storage | `write`/`fsync` error (EIO) | syscall return | log, retry once, then exit non-zero so supervisor restarts hub | `store: fdatasync: Input/output error` |
+| `supervisor` | itself killed | systemd (`Restart=always`) | systemd restarts it; it kills stale children via the pidfile/process group before relaunching | `sup: start, cleaned 3 stale children` |
+| any child | fd leak across restarts | hourly heartbeat records `/proc/<pid>/fd` count | soak evidence; regression test | `hb: ... fds=pird:5 micd:7 ...` |
+## 7. Interface: CLI (`src/cli`)
+Offline only: the CLI runs on the Pi (local console or USB-serial) and talks to
+the hub over `/run/pss/query.sock`. Four verbs, each with exact semantics:
+$ pss timeline [--since 08:00] [--until now]     # human-readable, one line per event
+09:41:07  ENTRY       routine     4m12s  latch+voice  [12 imgs, 30s audio]
+12:03:55  SOUND_ONLY  -             6s   voice        hallway?
+13:10:02  OFFLINE     -           38m   -            power lost
+15:22:40  ENTRY       UNEXPECTED   38s  latch         [20 imgs, 30s audio]
+$ pss events [--type entry|motion|sound] [--json]   # full records incl. scores, sensor flags
+$ pss status                                        # armed?, expected window, sensors OK/DEGRADED/SUSPECT
+$ pss health                                        # per-process uptime, restarts, RSS, fds, disk free, xruns, drops
+Plus two setters: `pss expect HH:MM-HH:MM` and `pss settime`.
+## 8. Constraints and substitutions
+| Ideal | What we use | What it costs us |
+| Small embedded I2S MEMS mic | Blue Snowball USB mic (owned) | Bulky; USB audio adds latency and xruns are possible; but unplugging it is a clean, safe fault to inject and demo |

+| Door reed switch for automatic ground truth | None installed (it is Macy's hotel door, not ours) | Ground truth comes from scripted trials and a paper log with timestamps; fewer labels and more effort |

+| Continuous video with pre-roll | JPEG still bursts on PIR trigger | Pi 5 has no hardware H.264 encoder; software video would take a large share of the CPU that audio analysis needs. We miss the first ~1 s (camera start latency, measured) and get frames, not motion |
+| Camera in the fusion | Camera as evidence only | We run no vision models (no pretrained models allowed and no budget to write one); images are for Macy to look at |

+| Battery power, so it can sit anywhere in the room | Wall outlet via a Pi 5 USB-C supply (5 V / 5 A) | Must sit within cable reach of an outlet; anyone, housekeeping included, can unplug it. That is a power cut, hence D and the `OFFLINE` gap record (Section 5) |
+| Reliable PIR-disconnect detection | Pull-up "stuck high" heuristic | Can be fooled; stated as a limitation |
+| Real hotel rooms | One test room (dorm/apartment) with a door | Acoustics and hallway noise are not a hotel's; claim narrowed accordingly |
+Replayed data: we will record labelled audio/PIR traces from scripted trials and
+replay them through `micd`'s feature path and the hub (`tools/replay`) to tune
+`K_imp`, `K_voice`, and `T_co`. Replayed data is labelled as such everywhere it
+appears; the soak and the demo run on live sensors.
+## 9. Evaluation plan
+| Measurement | Method | Target |

+| **B: PIR latency, IRQ vs. poll** | Drive a spare GPIO output into the PIR input line (PIR disconnected); toggle with a timestamp from the same monotonic clock; compute toggle → `pird` receipt. 1,000 edges per arm; arms: IRQ, poll 1/10/100 ms; idle and under `stress-ng --cpu 4` | IRQ p99 < 1 ms idle, < 5 ms loaded; report full CDFs |
+| **B: CPU cost** | `pird` CPU from `/proc/<pid>/stat` over 10 min each arm | IRQ ≈ 0 %; report poll cost |

+| **Detection accuracy (domain metric)** | ≥ 30 scripted trials each: real entry (door + walk in), housekeeping-style long entry, hallway noise only, non-human motion (fan-blown curtain), empty room. Paper log for ground truth | Confusion matrix; entry recall ≥ 90 %, false ENTRY on non-entry trials ≤ 5 % |
+| **Event-to-record latency** | PIR edge timestamp → event record durable | p95 < 5 s after window closes |
+| **D: power-cut recovery** | 20 power pulls at random times during clip and log writes | 0 corrupt records accepted; 0 dangling clip refs; lost data ≤ last open event |
+| **D: write volume** | bytes written per day from `/proc/<pid>/io` and `/sys/block/mmcblk0/stat` | report; < 1 GB/day at 20 entries/day |
+| **E: fault recovery** | `kill -9` each child 10×; unplug mic 10× for 10 min | detection < 1 s (crash) / < 15 s (hang); restart < 5 s; no fd growth |
+| **Camera start latency** | PIR edge → first JPEG mtime | report distribution (expected ~1 s) |
+| **Resource footprint** | hourly heartbeats over the 48 h soak: RSS, CPU, fds per process | flat RSS (< 1 MB drift after warm-up); plotted |
+## 10. Ownership map
+Owners are **to be decided by the team**; this table is the list to assign.
+Ownership means first authorship and answerability at the defense.
+| Subsystem | Path | Owner |
+| PIR capture + IRQ/poll comparison (B) | `src/capture/pir` | TBD |
+| Microphone capture + feature extraction | `src/capture/mic` | TBD |
+| Camera burst capture | `src/capture/cam` | TBD |
+| Storage layer (D) | `src/store` | TBD |
+| Analysis: background model, detectors, fusion FSM | `src/analysis` | TBD |
+| Hub (event loop, IPC server, query handling) | `src/hub` | Shared |
+| Supervisor (E) | `src/supervisor` | Shared |
+| CLI | `src/cli` | Shared |
+| Replay harness, plotting | `tools/` | TBD |
+Once decided, the same split goes into CLAUDE.md's Ownership section.
+## 11. AI-use plan and the no-network boundary
+**We use Claude Code for:** planning (plan mode first for every multi-file
+change), explaining APIs (libgpiod v2, ALSA, epoll, signalfd), drafting
+boilerplate, writing tests and fixtures, adversarial review of diffs, and
+debugging with pasted evidence (dmesg, `/proc/interrupts`, timing captures).
+**We do not use it for:** choosing detector thresholds or fusion rules without
+data we collected, or anything that runs on the device at runtime.
+**Boundary, legible in one minute.** The product links no network library and
+opens only AF_UNIX sockets. `make netcheck` greps `src/` for `AF_INET`,
+`AF_INET6`, `getaddrinfo`, `connect(` outside `AF_UNIX` helpers, `curl`, and
+`http`, and fails the build if any appear. The device runs with Wi-Fi and
+Ethernet disabled during the soak, which is the strongest possible check.
+## 12. Proposed repository layout
+src/capture/{pir,mic,cam}/   sensor daemons
+src/analysis/                features, background model, detectors, fusion
+src/store/                   event log, clip store, recovery, quota
+src/hub/                     event loop, IPC, query server
+src/supervisor/              process supervision, soak heartbeat
+src/cli/                     pss command
+src/common/                  IPC message structs, logging, heartbeat client
+tests/                       unit tests (store recovery, FSM, ring), run by `make test`
+tools/                       Python: replay harness, plotting (no graded mechanism)
+deploy/                      systemd unit for supervisor
+# Problem memo -- Portable Security (Owen Pendleton, Bryan Rosas>)
+## The user
+Macy Pendleton, who travels for work about 3 nights a month
+and stays in hotels and short-term rentals. They leave laptop, money,
+purses, etc in the room while out for most of the day.
+## The problem
+When Macy returns to the room, they have no way to know whether anyone
+entered, when, or for how long. Personal belongings like her purse
+had been moved, items seemed to be missing, and there was no way to
+establish what happened. Housekeeping visits are expected, but what's missing
+is a record that separates a routine visit from an unexpected one. The cost
+is worry on every trip that this may happen again and hundreds of dollars may
+be lost.
+## Why a device
+The room needs watching exactly when the traveler isn't in it, and their
+phone leaves with them. Commercial cameras (Wyze, Blink, Ring) need an
+app account and Wi-Fi, but hotel Wi-Fi typically requires a login page
+these cameras can't complete, and they upload footage to a company's
+cloud. Our device runs fully offline, keeps all data local, and produces
+a short list of entry events instead of hours of footage nobody reviews.
+## The sensors
+A PIR motion sensor, a microphone, and a camera. The microphone runs
+continuously into a short rolling buffer, and our code compares sound
+against the room's learned background noise. An entry is declared only
+when motion and a characteristic sound (door latch, voices) occur
+together, which filters out hallway noise and non-human motion. The
+camera then captures a short clip as evidence for confirmed events.
+## The mechanisms
+- B (interrupt-driven input): the PIR is read via a GPIO edge interrupt,
+  compared head-to-head against polling for latency and CPU cost, since
+  spinning on a pin that rarely changes takes CPU from the audio analysis
+  running on the same Pi.
+- D (custom storage layer): event clips and the event log must survive a
+  power cut mid-write and must not fill the SD card, so we need explicit
+  retention, write batching, and a crash-recovery story.
+## The risk
+Storage: audio and video clips can fill the SD card quickly over a
+48-hour run and wear it out with frequent writes. The other serious risk
+is building sound/motion fusion that beats a simple threshold without
+frequent false alarms.

# Portable Security System: team rules

## Commands
- Build: `make`    Cross/deploy: `make deploy PI=pi@<host>`
- Tests: `make test`    Sanitizers: `make asan`    Valgrind: `make memcheck`
- Network boundary check: `make netcheck` (fails if network code appears
  outside the hotspot UI server; see DESIGN.md Section 11)
- Soak sanity: `make soakcheck` (1-hour miniature of the 48h run)
- A change is DONE only when build, test, asan, and netcheck pass. Show output.

## Hard constraints
- The PRODUCT makes no network calls. Its only network code is the
  local UI server, bound to the Pi's own hotspot address (no internet
  uplink, no outbound connections). No LLM APIs, no cloud inference,
  no pretrained models. The intelligence in src/analysis is ours.
  This is a graded boundary.
- Every daemon must be supervisable: clean exit codes, no orphaned
  fds across restart, heartbeat within 60s of start.
- Every allocation checked; every syscall's error path handled and
  logged. The 48-hour soak is the test suite of last resort.
- NEVER weaken, skip, or delete a test to make the suite pass.

## Project facts (see DESIGN.md)
- Pi 5, wall powered (no battery). RTC backup battery is required: wall
  time across power cuts depends on it.
- Sensors: HC-SR501 PIR (GPIO), Blue Snowball USB mic (ALSA), OV5647
  camera (CSI, evidence only), arm button + LED (GPIO).
- Safe to hot-unplug for fault injection: the USB mic. The PIR only via
  its keyed connector. NEVER hot-unplug the CSI camera ribbon.

## Ownership
- Owen: capture daemons and arm button (src/capture/{pir,mic,cam})
- Bryan: storage layer, analysis engine (src/store, src/analysis)
- Shared: hub, supervisor, CLI, UI (src/hub, src/supervisor, src/cli, ui/)
- Each partner works in their own clone and their own Claude Code
  sessions; never prompt jointly in one session. Copy transcripts to
  CLAUDE-TRANSCRIPTS/<name>/ at every milestone.
- The agent edits outside the session owner's area only when told
  explicitly to.

## Style
- Systems core: C17, -Wall -Wextra -Werror, no VLAs.
  goto-cleanup for multi-resource functions.
- Python permitted only under tools/ and ui/. No graded mechanism
  may live there.
- Smallest diff that passes. Do not refactor unrelated code.

## Workflow
- Multi-file or algorithmic change: plan first, wait for approval.
- Hardware bugs: paste real evidence (dmesg, timing capture,
  /proc/interrupts). No fixes proposed from a verbal description.
- Commit only from a green state; message format "M<n>: <what>".

# Problem memo -- Portable Security (Owen Pendleton, Bryan Rosas>)

## The user
Macy Pendleton, who travels for work about 3 nights a month
and stays in hotels and short-term rentals. They leave laptop, money,
purses, etc in the room while out for most of the day.

## The problem
When Macy returns to the room, they have no way to know whether anyone
entered, when, or for how long. Personal belongings like her purse
had been moved, items seemed to be missing, and there was no way to 
establish what happened. Housekeeping visits are expected, but what's missing 
is a record that separates a routine visit from an unexpected one. The cost
is worry on every trip that this may happen again and hundreds of dollars may 
be lost.

## Why a device
The room needs watching exactly when the traveler isn't in it, and their
phone leaves with them. Commercial cameras (Wyze, Blink, Ring) need an
app account and Wi-Fi, but hotel Wi-Fi typically requires a login page
these cameras can't complete, and they upload footage to a company's
cloud. Our device runs fully offline, keeps all data local, and produces
a short list of entry events instead of hours of footage nobody reviews.

## The sensors
A PIR motion sensor, a microphone, and a camera. The microphone runs
continuously into a short rolling buffer, and our code compares sound
against the room's learned background noise. An entry is declared only
when motion and a characteristic sound (door latch, voices) occur
together, which filters out hallway noise and non-human motion. The
camera then captures a short clip as evidence for confirmed events.

## The mechanisms
- B (interrupt-driven input): the PIR is read via a GPIO edge interrupt,
  compared head-to-head against polling for latency and CPU cost, since
  spinning on a pin that rarely changes takes CPU from the audio analysis
  running on the same Pi.
- D (custom storage layer): event clips and the event log must survive a
  power cut mid-write and must not fill the SD card, so we need explicit
  retention, write batching, and a crash-recovery story.

## The risk
Storage: audio and video clips can fill the SD card quickly over a
48-hour run and wear it out with frequent writes. The other serious risk
is building sound/motion fusion that beats a simple threshold without
frequent false alarms.

# Problem memo -- Portable Security (Owen Pendleton, Bryan Rosas)

## The user
Macy Pendleton, who travels for work about 3 nights a month and stays in
hotels and short-term rentals. She leaves her laptop, cash, and bags in
the room while she is out for most of the day.

## The problem
When Macy returns to the room, she has no way to know whether anyone
entered, when, or for how long. Her purse has been moved, items have
seemed to be missing, and there was no way to establish what happened.
Housekeeping visits are expected; what's missing is a record that
separates a routine visit from an unexpected one. The cost is worry on
every trip and, when something does go missing, hundreds of dollars.

## Why a device
The room needs watching exactly when Macy isn't in it, and her phone
leaves with her. Cloud cameras (Wyze, Blink, Ring) need an account and
Wi-Fi, but hotel Wi-Fi usually needs a login page these cameras can't
complete, and they upload footage to a company's cloud. An old phone
running a motion app records hours of video nobody reviews, can't tell
an entry from a curtain moving, and dies when its battery or the app
does. A $15 door-stop alarm only makes noise when Macy isn't there to
hear it, and leaves no record. Our device runs fully offline, keeps all
data local, and gives Macy a short list of entry events when she returns.

## The sensors
A PIR motion sensor and a microphone cooperate; a camera adds evidence.
The microphone runs continuously, and our code compares sound against
the room's learned background noise. An entry is declared only when
motion and a characteristic sound (door latch, voices) occur together,
which filters out hallway noise and non-human motion. The camera then
captures still images as evidence for confirmed entries.

## The mechanisms
- B (interrupt-driven input): the PIR is read via a GPIO edge interrupt,
  compared head-to-head against polling for latency and CPU cost.
- D (custom storage layer): the event log and clips must survive a power
  cut mid-write and must not fill the SD card.
- (Added in the design document: E, multi-process supervision, because a
  monitor that silently dies is worse than none.)

## The risk
Storage: audio and image clips can fill the SD card over a 48-hour run
and wear it out. The other serious risk is building sound/motion fusion
that beats a simple threshold without frequent false alarms.

# Design Document: Portable Security (Owen Pendleton, Bryan Rosas)

**Milestone:** M2. **Status:** draft for review. M5's version will carry a
changelog of what this one got wrong.

## 1. Summary

Macy travels about three nights a month and leaves a laptop, cash, and bags in
a hotel room all day. Our device sits in the room while she is out and, when
she returns, answers one question with a short timeline: *did anyone come in,
when, and for how long?* It has no internet connection, no cloud, and no
account; every byte stays on its SD card. Macy reads the timeline from her
phone over the device's own Wi-Fi hotspot.

**The narrowed claim:** in a test room, the device separates *door-entry
events* (motion plus a door/voice sound signature) from *motion-only* and
*sound-only* events with a measured confusion matrix, and keeps a
crash-consistent record of them through power cuts and sensor faults.

**Mechanisms:** **B** interrupt-driven GPIO input (PIR and arm button) vs.
polling; **D** a crash-consistent storage layer; **E** multi-process
supervision.

**Hardware:** Raspberry Pi 5 with RTC backup battery · HC-SR501 PIR (GPIO,
keyed connector) · Blue Snowball USB microphone (ALSA) · Arducam OV5647 (CSI,
Pi 5 22-pin cable) · arm button + LED (GPIO). PIR and microphone are the two
*cooperating* sensors; the camera only collects evidence for confirmed entries.

## 2. Architecture

```
 PIR + button (GPIO)    Blue Snowball (USB)        OV5647 (CSI)
     | GPIO edges           | USB isoc audio           | CSI-2
=====|======================|==========================|===================== kernel
 RP1 gpiochip            snd-usb-audio             libcamera
 (kernel timestamps)     (44.1 kHz s16 = 88.2 KB/s)
=====|======================|==========================|===================== user
     v                      v                          v
 +--------+           +-----------+             +-----------+
 |  pird  |           |   micd    |             |   camd    |
 | PIR +  |           | 20 ms FFT |             | burst on  |
 | button |           | features; |             | trigger,  |
 | + LED  |           | 15 s PCM  |             | ~2 fps    |
 +--------+           | ring      |             +-----------+
     | edge/button    +-----------+   trigger (<1/min) ^  | frame-ready
     | msgs <1 Hz,          | features 50 Hz x 64 B    |  | 2 Hz, path only
     | ~40 B                | = 3.2 KB/s               |  v
 +--------------------------------------------------------------+
 |                     hub (single writer)                      |
 |  analysis/: background model -> detectors -> fusion FSM      |
 |  store/: event log + stats log (append, CRC) + clip store    |
 |  arm state machine; query socket                             |
 +--------------------------------------------------------------+
     | events ~0.1-20/hr (fsync on open and close); clips ~6-9 MB
     | per confirmed entry; stats 1/min batched
     v
 SD card: /var/lib/pss/{events/, stats/, clips/}

 supervisor (E): fork/execs pird, micd, camd, hub, ui; 5 s heartbeats from
 each over AF_UNIX; hourly soak heartbeat (liveness, RSS, fds, counts).

 Macy's phone --Wi-Fi (hotspot, no uplink)--> ui (read-only page) --AF_UNIX--> hub
 pss (CLI, over SSH on the hotspot) --AF_UNIX query socket (~1/min)--> hub
```

All internal IPC is AF_UNIX `SOCK_SEQPACKET`: message boundaries are kept, and
a dead peer shows up as EOF/EPIPE, which is the fault signal E needs.

| Process | Threads | Inputs → outputs |
|---|---|---|
| `supervisor` | 1 (epoll: signalfd, child sockets, timerfd) | heartbeats → restarts, soak log |
| `pird` | 1 (blocks on GPIO edge events, or `timerfd` in poll mode) | PIR/button edges → msgs; LED |
| `micd` | 2: ALSA capture + feature thread, joined by an SPSC ring | PCM → features; audio clip on request |
| `camd` | 1 + `rpicam-still` child per burst | trigger → JPEGs in `clips/*.tmp` |
| `hub` | 1 (epoll over child + query sockets, timerfd) | features + edges → events, storage |
| `ui` | 1 (Python, `ui/`, display only) | HTTP on hotspot address → hub queries |

All run at default priority; mechanism C is not claimed.

## 3. Mechanism mapping

### B: Interrupt-driven GPIO input (`pird`, `src/capture/pir`)
**Implementation.** `pird` requests the PIR and button lines through libgpiod
v2 with both edges and kernel timestamps (`CLOCK_MONOTONIC`), and blocks until
the RP1 GPIO interrupt delivers an edge. A `--poll=<ms>` mode reads line values
on a `timerfd` instead; that is the comparison arm.
**Why Macy needs it.** The device sits idle for hours and must catch the few
edges that matter. An interrupt reports every edge with the kernel's
timestamp; a poll only knows a change happened somewhere in the last interval,
and can miss a button press shorter than that interval entirely. A 10 ms poll
also wakes the CPU 100 times a second for a sensor that changes a few times a
day. We are honest about scale: the PIR itself takes hundreds of milliseconds
to react to motion, and on a Pi 5 the CPU difference may be small. We will
report whatever we measure.
**Measured.** Edge-to-userspace latency distribution, missed short pulses, and
`pird` CPU, IRQ vs. poll at 1, 10, 100 ms, idle and under load (Section 9).

### D: Crash-consistent storage (`src/store`, linked into `hub`)
**Implementation.** Append-only CRC32-framed logs in segment files (events and
stats kept separately); atomic clip commits (tmp → fsync → rename → fsync dir);
recovery at startup; byte quota with oldest-first clip eviction (Section 5).
**Why Macy needs it.** The device runs from a hotel wall outlet, and outlets
get used: housekeeping unplugs things to vacuum, Macy unplugs it to pack, and
an intruder may pull the plug on purpose. The record exists to answer "did
someone come in?" after the fact, so it must survive exactly that.
**Measured.** Power-pull recovery (records lost, corrupt records accepted,
dangling clip references), bytes written per day, fsync count and latency.

### E: Multi-process supervision (`src/supervisor`)
**Implementation.** One process per sensor, plus hub, ui, and supervisor.
Children heartbeat every 5 s. The supervisor restarts any child that exits or
misses heartbeats for 15 s (SIGKILL first), with backoff 1 s → 60 s that resets
after 10 min healthy. Exit code `3` means "device gone": the supervisor retries
every 30 s and the hub marks that sensor DEGRADED instead of storming restarts.
**Why Macy needs it.** A security monitor that silently dies is worse than
none, because Macy believes it is on duty. If the camera hangs or the mic drops
off USB, the PIR record must keep flowing and the timeline must say which
sensors were offline and when.
**Measured.** `kill -9` each child and unplug the mic: detection time, recovery
time, events lost during the gap, log excerpts.

## 4. Analysis engine (`src/analysis`, all ours)

**Audio features (in `micd`).** 20 ms hops (882 samples) over a 1024-point Hann
window. Per frame: RMS, energy in 8 log-spaced bands (100 Hz – 8 kHz), and
spectral flux. FFT is a primitive (small library or our own radix-2).

**Background model.** Per band, an exponentially weighted mean and variance
(time constant ~60 s), updated only outside active events so a conversation
doesn't become "background". Frames are scored as per-band z-scores, so the
same device works next to a loud HVAC unit and in a silent room.

**Detectors.**
- *Impulse (latch/door):* spectral-flux z-score above `K_imp`, broadband, decay
  under 150 ms.
- *Voice:* z-score in the 300–3400 Hz bands above `K_voice` for ≥ 400 ms within
  2 s, with sub-200 Hz energy not dominant (rules out HVAC).
- *PIR:* HC-SR501 in **single-trigger mode** with the delay pot at minimum, so
  each detection is a pulse of a few seconds followed by a ~2.5 s low block
  time, even under continuous motion. A person moving around produces a train
  of pulses.

**Fusion state machine (in `hub`).**
```
IDLE --PIR rise--> MOTION_WINDOW (±T_co = 3 s around the edge; audio history checked)
MOTION_WINDOW --impulse or voice in window--> ENTRY (confirmed; durable at once)
MOTION_WINDOW --window expires, no audio--> MOTION_ONLY
IDLE --impulse/voice, no PIR within ±T_co--> SOUND_ONLY (hallway)
ENTRY/MOTION_ONLY --no PIR pulse and no voice for T_quiet = 30 s--> close event
```
Opening and closing use different conditions, so ten minutes of someone moving
around is one event, not forty.

**Arm state machine (in `hub`, button handled by `pird`).**
```
DISARMED --button--> EXIT_DELAY (60 s, LED blinks) --> ARMED (LED off)
ARMED --ENTRY confirmed--> GRACE (30 s) --button--> DISARMED, entry labelled `owner`
GRACE --30 s, no button--> ARMED, entry reported (routine / UNEXPECTED)
```
Events are only reported while ARMED. Macy can also use `pss arm` /
`pss disarm`. The LED stays dark while armed so the device doesn't draw
attention.

**Routine vs. unexpected (optional).** Housekeeping times are often unknown,
so the expected window is optional (`pss expect 10:00-14:00`). With no window,
every confirmed entry while armed is reported plainly; with one, entries
inside it are labelled `routine` and others `UNEXPECTED`. The device never
tries to identify who entered.

**Why a threshold cannot do this.** A loudness threshold fires on every
hallway door slam and misses a quiet entry in a noisy room; a PIR alone fires
on curtains moved by HVAC. The decision rests on the *timing* of two different
physical signals, scored against a background learned in *this* room, with
hysteresis on event boundaries. No single `if` reproduces that.

## 5. Storage and data

| Data | Rate | Format | Retention |
|---|---|---|---|
| Event records | ~0.1–20/hr | `[len u32][type u16][ver u16][payload][crc32]` | kept (tiny); never evicted |
| Stats / heartbeat records | 1/min, batched | same framing, separate segments | whole segments deleted after 7 days |
| Audio clips (confirmed entries) | 10 s pre-roll + ≤ 20 s post ≈ 2.6 MB | WAV | clip quota, oldest first |
| Image bursts (confirmed entries) | ~2 fps × 10 s ≈ 3–6 MB | JPEG | clip quota, oldest first |
| Daemon text logs | low | timestamped lines | logrotate, 4 × 5 MB |

**Event log.** Segments `events/seg-NNNNNN.pel`, capped at 4 MB. When an ENTRY
is confirmed, an `event_open` record is appended and `fdatasync`ed
immediately; `event_close` is synced when the event ends. So if someone pulls
the plug mid-entry, the entry is already on disk. Recovery turns an open
without a close into an event marked `interrupted (power lost)`.
MOTION_ONLY and SOUND_ONLY events are written once, at close.

**Stats log.** Separate segments in `stats/`, buffered in memory and flushed
once a minute. A power cut loses at most a minute of stats, never an event.
Because stats live apart from events, old stats are dropped by deleting whole
segments, with no compaction.

**Clips.** Written as `clips/<event-id>.{wav,dir}.tmp`; on completion: fsync
file → rename → fsync directory. The record referencing a clip is written only
after the rename is durable, so the log never points at a missing clip. Bursts
for unconfirmed events are deleted. The `micd` PCM ring holds 15 s, so a full
10 s pre-roll still exists after the ~3 s confirmation delay.

**Recovery (hub start).** For the newest event and stats segments: stop at the
first bad length or CRC, `ftruncate` there, and log `store: recovered seg=N
valid=R truncated_bytes=B`. Delete every `clips/*.tmp` and log each. Close any
open entry as `interrupted`. Rebuild the in-memory index.

**Power-loss gaps.** The hub writes a `boot` record at every start. The gap
between the last durable stats record and `boot` is when the device was off,
accurate to about a minute; the timeline shows it as `OFFLINE` so Macy doesn't
read silence as "nobody came in".

**Quota.** Default 2 GiB for `clips/` (~250 entries). Before each clip, evict
the oldest clips until there is room. Below a 5 % free-space floor, clips stop
and event records continue.

**Time.** There is no NTP offline. Wall time comes from the Pi 5's RTC, and the
RTC backup battery is a **requirement**: `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` restarts at every
boot, so after a power cut only the RTC knows how long the device was off.
Records carry both clocks; intervals and ordering use monotonic time within a
boot. If the RTC reports an unset clock at boot, the hub logs it and the
timeline shows the gap as `OFFLINE (duration unknown)` until the clock is set
(`pss settime`, or the "set clock from this phone" button on the UI page).

## 6. Failure-mode table

| Component | Failure | Detected by | System response | Log shows |
|---|---|---|---|---|

| `micd` | crash / `kill -9` | `SIGCHLD` + `waitpid` | restart with backoff; gap events tagged DEGRADED | `sup: micd killed by signal 9, restart #3 in 1s` |
| `micd` | ALSA overrun | `-EPIPE` | `snd_pcm_prepare`, count, continue | `micd: xrun #N recovered` |
| `pird` | crash / hang | `SIGCHLD` / 15 s missed heartbeat | SIGKILL + restart; PIR DEGRADED | `sup: pird heartbeat missed 15s, SIGKILL` |
| PIR | unplugged at its connector | pull-up holds line high; in single-trigger mode a real pulse never lasts past `T_pulse + 5 s` (to verify on bench) | PIR SUSPECT within ~10 s; the one false edge becomes MOTION_ONLY (no sound) and is tagged `possible-unplug` | `pird: line high 10s > max pulse, SUSPECT` |
| PIR | warm-up false triggers | uptime < 60 s | ignore edges | `pird: warm-up, edges ignored until T+60s` |
| `camd` | `rpicam-still` fails | non-zero exit, missing files | event kept, tagged `no-images` | `camd: rpicam-still exit 255; burst skipped` |
| `camd` | crash / `kill -9` | `SIGCHLD` | restart; stale `.tmp` cleaned | `sup: camd killed by signal 9` |
| camera | ribbon unplugged | n/a | **not a supported fault**: CSI must never be hot-unplugged | n/a |
| `hub` | crash / `kill -9` | `SIGCHLD` | restart; recovery runs; daemons reconnect with backoff, counting dropped frames | `store: recovered seg=12 valid=341 truncated_bytes=58` |
| `ui` | crash | `SIGCHLD` | restart; detection unaffected | `sup: ui exited 1, restart in 1s` |
| storage | power cut mid-write | CRC/length at startup | truncate torn tail; delete `.tmp`; close open entry as `interrupted` | as above |
| power | unplugged (anyone) | gap before next `boot` record | timeline `OFFLINE` span | `hub: boot after power loss, offline 10:02-10:40 (38m)` |
| clock | RTC battery missing/dead | RTC unset at boot | gap shown as duration unknown | `hub: RTC unset, offline duration unknown` |
